findings.issue: Only the documentation stops anyone from enabling the IP check behind the current gateway. If an operator sets USER_REFERRAL_IP_LOOKBACK > 0 against the docs, the round-3 defect comes back with nothing in the logs: the gateway IP gets hashed, genuine same-gateway claims are refused and farming is not limited. The impact is limited to wrongly refused or allowed referral claims, and it needs the documentation to be ignored.
findings.fix: Optional until B-1 (F-20261119-03) lands: log a startup WARN when ip-lookback > 0 that names backlog B-1 and the gateway client-IP requirement, or have B-1 add a guard that ties enabling the check to the trusted gateway header.

summary: Approve. I reviewed review-delta.diff (78a7b4f6..2b229705) in full and checked the worktree source. With the default config, the round-3 major is neutralised. application.yml defaults USER_REFERRAL_IP_LOOKBACK to 0 and the UserProperties field default is Duration.ZERO, so a blank env value also gives 0. ReferralService.view records IP activity only when lookback > 0. claim computes no HMAC and stores claim_ip_hash as NULL when the check is off, and refuseIfAbusive skips the network query. A negative lookback also counts as off. No Helm or Compose file sets the variable. The new ReferralIpCheckDefaultOffIntegrationTest proves that a same-IP claim succeeds and that no activity row or claim hash is written by default. The tests that cover the check-on path now set ip-lookback=30d explicitly, so that coverage is kept. The referral code-age check is unchanged and stays on: it is a parameterised SQL comparison against server time, with the 10m default. HMAC and salt handling is unchanged. When the check is off no IP is hashed, so the per-process random key (TD-P8-24) does not matter for now. Retention is unchanged: the 30d purge under the job lock, and clearing on account deletion, still apply to any rows written while the check was on. I found no IP values in logs and no new endpoints, auth changes, dependencies or ledger paths in the delta. The gateway Helm SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none change is unchanged from round 3, where it was judged safe. The documentation clearly says not to enable the check behind the current gateway: env-descriptions.json, environment-variables.md, the UserProperties javadoc, the application.yml comment, the phase-08 doc and remediation-plan row 37 all state it, and they point to backlog B-1. My round-3 minor finding (OIDC callback relies on stripped X-Forwarded-*) is now filed as TD-SEC-15 with remediation row 56. There are two remaining minor findings. One is a documentation inconsistency about the retention variable. The other is that nothing in the running service, beyond the docs, stops the check being enabled before B-1 lands.
